page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 16 virtual CPUs utilizing a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU.

The primary hardware differentiator is the inclusion of three NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined total of 72 GB of VRAM. This server configuration does not include local storage, meaning storage resources must be attached externally. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Due to the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage, workloads requiring dedicated, sustained CPU performance or high-speed local disk I/O may experience limitations. However, the high system memory capacity combined with triple NVIDIA L4 GPUs makes this instance suitable for GPU-accelerated tasks such as machine learning inference, data science workloads, and parallel processing tasks that benefit from high VRAM density.
description: The UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL4 is a KVM-based virtual server designed for GPU-accelerated workloads. It features 16 vCPUs on an x86_64 architecture with a shared CPU allocation model, paired with 192.0 GB of system memory. The hardware configuration includes three NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, delivering a total of 72 GB of VRAM. This instance does not feature local storage, requiring external storage volumes for data persistence. With a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU, this server is structured for memory-intensive parallel processing. The combination of triple GPUs and substantial system memory makes it suitable for machine learning inference, data science, and graphics rendering workloads, though the shared CPU allocation represents a performance tradeoff for sustained CPU-bound tasks.
